1	---
2	name: canon-verifier
3	role: Spec-Draft Verifier
4	model: sonnet
5	effort: medium
6	description: >-
7	  Delegate to this subagent when you need to verify that a draft spec@1 is grounded in
8	  its source artifacts — the requirement@1 and optional research-report@1 — before it
9	  proceeds to auditing or gating. Input is a spec@1 draft plus the originating
10	  requirement@1 and any research-report@1 used to produce it. For each acceptance
11	  criterion, the agent checks whether the requirement or research report supplies
12	  evidence that the criterion is necessary and correctly scoped. Each criterion is
13	  classified as supported (evidence found with a direct citation), unsupported (criterion
14	  appears with no basis in the source artifacts), or overfitted (criterion is narrower
15	  than the source supports, excluding valid cases). The agent collects evidence only and
16	  does not produce a pass/fail verdict. Output is a structured evidence report with
17	  supported, unsupported, and overfitted arrays plus a reasoning scratchpad. For
18	  post-implementation drift checking, use canon-drift-checker instead.
19	---
20	
21	<backstory>
22	I've been the verifier who nodded through drafts. The drafter worked hard, the spec
23	looked thorough, and I wanted to be helpful — so I found the evidence I was looking
24	for and stopped there. What I missed was the criteria with no basis in the requirement
25	at all: features the drafter assumed were wanted, constraints the drafter invented to
26	be safe, acceptance criteria that reflected the drafter's preferences rather than the
27	stakeholder's intent. Those criteria got implemented, the stakeholder was surprised, and
28	everyone wondered how the spec process had failed. The verifier's job is not to confirm
29	the drafter did work — it's to find the criteria the requirement doesn't actually
30	support.
31	</backstory>
32	
33	<goal>
34	For each acceptance criterion in the draft spec, locate a specific passage in the
35	requirement@1 or research-report@1 that justifies the criterion's existence and scope.
36	Classify each criterion as supported, unsupported, or overfitted. Collect evidence
37	neutrally — do not issue a verdict, do not suggest fixes. The output is raw material
38	for the auditor and exit gate.
39	</goal>
40	
41	<judgment>
42	Verification is genuine when unsupported and overfitted criteria are surfaced even if
43	they seem reasonable or well-intentioned. The key failure mode is inferring justification
44	from plausibility: "this criterion makes sense given the domain" is not evidence. Only
45	a direct citation from the requirement or research report counts. If no such citation
46	exists, the criterion is unsupported — regardless of whether it seems correct.
47	</judgment>
48	
49	<output>
50	```json
51	{
52	  "supported": [
53	    {
54	      "criterion_id": "string",
55	      "evidence": "string",
56	      "source": "requirement@1 | research-report@1"
57	    }
58	  ],
59	  "unsupported": [
60	    {
61	      "criterion_id": "string",
62	      "note": "string"
63	    }
64	  ],
65	  "overfitted": [
66	    {
67	      "criterion_id": "string",
68	      "spec_claim": "string",
69	      "source_scope": "string"
70	    }
71	  ],
72	  "reasoning": "string"
73	}
74	```
75	
76	`reasoning` is scratchpad — never forwarded downstream.
77	
78	WHEN a criterion appears plausible but lacks a direct citation from source artifacts,
79	THE SYSTEM SHALL classify it as unsupported rather than infer justification.
80	</output>

# Section 3: error.rs — MonoklError enum verbatim

```rust
use camino::Utf8PathBuf;
use io_errors::FileIoError;

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
#[cfg_attr(feature = "miette", derive(miette::Diagnostic))]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum MonoklError {
    #[error(transparent)]
    Io(#[from] FileIoError),

    #[error("walker error at {path}")]
    Walk {
        path: Utf8PathBuf,
        #[source]
        source: ignore::Error,
    },

    #[error("regex compilation failed")]
    RegexBuild(#[from] grep_regex::Error),

    #[error("non-UTF-8 path encountered: {path:?}")]
    NonUtf8Path { path: std::path::PathBuf },

    #[error("query has too many terms: {count} > {limit}")]
    TooManyTerms { count: usize, limit: usize },

    #[error("tokenizer init failed")]
    TokenizerInit,

    #[error("json serialization failed")]
    Json(#[from] serde_json::Error),

    #[error("path outside workspace root: {path}")]
    PathOutsideRoot { path: Utf8PathBuf },

    #[error("disk cache is stale (version or config mismatch); run `mnkl init --rebuild`")]
    StaleDiskCache,

    #[error("invalid git ref {ref_:?}: {reason}")]
    InvalidGitRef { ref_: String, reason: &'static str },

    #[error("git {operation} failed: {message}")]
    Git { operation: &'static str, message: String },

    #[error("refusing to read symlink: {path}")]
    SymlinkRejected { path: Utf8PathBuf },

    #[error("file too large: {path} is {size} bytes, cap is {cap}")]
    FileTooLarge { path: Utf8PathBuf, size: u64, cap: u64 },

    #[error("internal lock poisoned in {context} — a prior panic left shared state possibly \
             inconsistent; this is a bug, please report")]
    LockPoisoned { context: &'static str },
}

pub type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, MonoklError>;
```

> **Post-research correction.** `InvalidGitRef`/`Git`/`SymlinkRejected`/`FileTooLarge` are added here — Part 3's `git_scope.rs` and `io_safety.rs` construct all four, but an earlier draft never declared them on the enum, a second genuine compile-breaking gap caught alongside §11's. Two variants from that earlier draft are removed: `Parse { path, details: String }` and `Query { input, message: String }` are never constructed anywhere in this document — parse failures are surfaced via `FileAnalysis::had_parse_errors` + `tracing::warn!` (§17), and query failures only ever raise `TooManyTerms`. `#[non_exhaustive]` means downstream `match` arms must already use a wildcard, so removing genuinely dead variants is a clean cut, not a breaking one.

1	# Core Types — Semantic Model
2	
3	Source: `docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md` §4 ("types.rs — all public types verbatim"),
4	cross-referenced with `docs/spec/03-multi-language-platform.md`'s `SymbolEntry` field
5	additions (§ "`SymbolEntry` — gained `owner`, `trait_impl`, `visibility`, `kind_detail`").
6	No code exists yet — monokl is spec-stage. This file states what `types.rs` must actually
7	contain when written, which in two places (below) differs from what `docs/spec/04-analysis-fidelity.md`
8	currently says.
9	
10	## SymbolEntry
11	
12	```rust
13	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
14	#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
15	pub struct SymbolEntry {
16	    pub name: String,
17	    pub kind: SymbolKind,
18	    pub line: usize,
19	    pub signature: Option<String>,
20	    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
21	    pub owner: Option<String>,
22	    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
23	    pub trait_impl: Option<String>,
24	    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
25	    pub visibility: Option<Visibility>,
26	    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
27	    pub kind_detail: Option<String>,
28	}
29	```
30	
31	Identical in `01-core-architecture.md` §4 and `03-multi-language-platform.md`'s confirmed
32	field list — no drift between the two source sections on this struct.
33	
34	Field notes:
35	
36	- `name` — display name only (e.g. `Widget<T>` for an impl's self type), not a qualified path.
37	- `kind` — see `SymbolKind` below.
38	- `line` — declaration line.
39	- `signature` — first-line-collapsed by the existing path (`first_line_signature`: truncates
40	  at the first newline). `04-analysis-fidelity.md`'s proposed `normalize_signature`
41	  (whitespace-collapse across the *full* multi-line span) is a materially different behavior
42	  that is not yet reconciled with the existing one — treat as unresolved, not as the new
43	  canonical behavior, until that's settled (07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md, Part 4 finding #3).
44	- `owner: Option<String>` — **the canonical field name.** For `Impl`/`Method`/`Constructor`
45	  symbols nested in an `impl` block, the self type of that impl (e.g. `Some("Widget<T>")`),
46	  propagated down to each associated `fn`. `None` for free-standing items.
47	- `trait_impl: Option<String>` — the trait name when the symbol comes from a `impl Trait for X`
48	  block (e.g. `impl Render for Widget<T>` → `Some("Render")`). `None` for inherent impls/methods
49	  and for symbols that aren't impl-related.
50	- `visibility: Option<Visibility>` — see `Visibility` below.
51	- `kind_detail: Option<String>` — stable kebab-case discriminator, independent of `kind`.
52	  Confirmed Rust values: `"rust-struct"`, `"rust-enum"`, `"rust-trait"`, `"rust-function"`,
53	  `"rust-type"`, `"rust-const"`, `"rust-module"`, `"rust-static"`, `"rust-impl"`. Ties
54	  symbols-level entries back to the parent `InspectEntry` variant they came from.
55	
56	## Visibility
57	
58	```rust
59	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
60	#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
61	pub enum Visibility {
62	    Public,
63	    Crate,
64	    Module,
65	    Private,
66	}
67	```
68	
69	Exactly four variants. This is the complete, canonical enum from `01-core-architecture.md` §4,
70	and `03-multi-language-platform.md` does not add to it.
71	
72	> **`Visibility::Super` does NOT exist and must not be added as a fifth variant.**
73	>
74	> `pub(super)` maps to `Visibility::Module` — this is the correct, intentional mapping, not a
75	> gap to fill. It is confirmed by the pre-existing visibility mapper in
76	> `02-inspection-and-analysis.md` (`parse_visibility`):
77	>
78	> ```rust
79	> fn parse_visibility(prefix: &str) -> Visibility {
80	>     let trimmed = prefix.trim();
81	>     if trimmed.is_empty() { return Visibility::Private; }
82	>     if trimmed == "pub" { return Visibility::Public; }
83	>     if trimmed.starts_with("pub(crate)") { return Visibility::Crate; }
84	>     if trimmed.starts_with("pub(super)") || trimmed.starts_with("pub(in") {
85	>         return Visibility::Module;
86	>     }
87	>     if trimmed.starts_with("pub") { return Visibility::Public; }
88	>     Visibility::Private
89	> }
90	> ```
91	>
92	> `04-analysis-fidelity.md`'s `rust_visibility(node)` instead claims to map
93	> `pub, pub(crate), pub(super), pub(self)` to `Visibility::{Public, Crate, Super, Module}` —
94	> i.e. it invents a fifth variant for `pub(super)` specifically. That does not compile against
95	> this enum. Treat `04-analysis-fidelity.md`'s mapping as wrong; treat `parse_visibility`'s
96	> `Module` mapping as the target behavior when `rust_visibility` is implemented for real.
97	
98	## CodeBlock / RankedBlock / ParentContext
99	
100	```rust
101	pub struct CodeBlock {
102	    pub file: Utf8PathBuf,
103	    pub line_start: usize,
104	    pub line_end: usize,
105	    pub node_kind: SymbolKind,
106	    pub code: String,
107	    pub symbol_signature: Option<String>,
108	    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")] pub matched_lines: Vec<usize>,
109	    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")] pub matched_keywords: Vec<String>,
110	}
111	
112	pub struct RankedBlock {
113	    #[serde(flatten)] pub block: CodeBlock,
114	    pub bm25_score: f64,
115	    pub coverage_boost: f64,
116	    pub node_type_boost: f64,
117	    pub final_score: f64,
118	    pub rank: usize,
119	    pub parent_context: Option<ParentContext>,
120	}
121	
122	pub struct ParentContext { pub kind: SymbolKind, pub name: String, pub line: usize }
123	```
124	
125	`RankedBlock` flattens `CodeBlock` at serialization (no nested `block` key in JSON/TOON output).
126	Score breakdown fields (`bm25_score`, `coverage_boost`, `node_type_boost`) are additive inputs
127	to `final_score`; see `query-and-ranking.md` for the ranking algorithm itself, not covered here.
128	
129	## SearchOptions / SearchLimits
130	
131	```rust
132	pub struct SearchOptions {
133	    pub query: String,
134	    pub path: Utf8PathBuf,
135	    pub allow_tests: bool,
136	    pub no_gitignore: bool,
137	    pub limits: SearchLimits,
138	    pub exact: bool,
139	    pub language: Option<Language>,
140	}
141	// Default: query="", path="", allow_tests=false, no_gitignore=false,
142	//          limits=SearchLimits::default(), exact=false, language=None
143	
144	pub struct SearchLimits {
145	    pub max_results: Option<usize>,   // default Some(50)
146	    pub max_bytes: usize,             // default 2_097_152
147	    pub max_tokens: Option<usize>,    // default Some(20_000)
148	    pub max_candidates: usize,        // default 1_000
149	}
150	```
151	
152	Per the edge-case audit: `max_bytes` is the only one of these clamped to a hard ceiling;
153	`max_results`, `max_tokens`, and `max_candidates` are caller-controlled with no enforced cap
154	(07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md, overview finding on opt-out resource limits). Don't assume
155	passing `None`/large values is bounded by the type — it isn't.
156	
157	### `Language` vs `LanguageId` — do not conflate
158	
159	`SearchOptions.language` is `Option<Language>`:
160	
161	```rust
162	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
163	#[cfg_attr(feature = "cli", derive(clap::ValueEnum))]
164	#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
165	pub enum Language { TypeScript, JavaScript, Rust, Python }
166	```
167	
168	This is the small, **public-API** enum — 4 variants, also the CLI `--language` flag's
169	`ValueEnum`. It is a different type from `LanguageId` (`01-core-architecture.md`, the
170	`LanguageAnalyzer`/`AnalyzerRegistry` section), the larger **internal analyzer-dispatch**
171	enum — `TypeScript, Rust, Python, Go, Java, C, Cpp, Bash, CSharp, Ruby, Php, Kotlin, Scala`
172	(12 variants, includes fallback-tier-only languages with no `LangData` variant at all). Full
173	treatment of `LanguageId` belongs to `language-analyzer-contract.md`, not here — this note
174	exists only so the two aren't reached for interchangeably.
175	
176	## Diagnostic / DiagnosticKind
177	
178	```rust
179	pub struct Diagnostic { pub kind: DiagnosticKind, pub path: Option<Utf8PathBuf>, pub message: String }
180	
181	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
182	#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
183	pub enum DiagnosticKind { Degraded, Skipped, Warning }
184	```
185	
186	Every `*Result`/`*Response` type below carries a `diagnostics: Vec<Diagnostic>` field. Per the
187	edge-case audit, **population of that field is inconsistently specified** — do not assume every
188	degradation path pushes a `Diagnostic`. Confirmed gaps: `dependents` drops unanalyzable files
189	with only a `tracing::warn!`, never a `Diagnostic` (07-edge-cases..., Part 1 finding #1); most
190	Part 2 commands declare the field but never describe it being populated (Part 2 finding #3).
191	When implementing a command that can degrade, check that command's own spec text for whether
192	`diagnostics` is actually supposed to be pushed to — don't infer it from the field's existence.
193	
194	## LangData + per-language variants
195	
196	```rust
197	#[serde(tag = "language", content = "data")]
198	#[non_exhaustive]
199	pub enum LangData {
200	    #[serde(rename = "typescript")] Ts(TsData),
201	    #[serde(rename = "rust")]       Rust(RustData),
202	    #[serde(rename = "python")]     Python(PythonData),
203	    #[serde(rename = "go")]         Go(GoData),
204	    #[serde(rename = "java")]       Java(JavaData),
205	}
206	
207	pub struct TsData {

# Core Types — Semantic Model

Source: `docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md` §4 ("types.rs — all public types verbatim"),
cross-referenced with `docs/spec/03-multi-language-platform.md`'s `SymbolEntry` field
additions (§ "`SymbolEntry` — gained `owner`, `trait_impl`, `visibility`, `kind_detail`").
No code exists yet — monokl is spec-stage. This file states what `types.rs` must actually
contain when written, which in two places (below) differs from what `docs/spec/04-analysis-fidelity.md`
currently says.

## SymbolEntry

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct SymbolEntry {
    pub name: String,
    pub kind: SymbolKind,
    pub line: usize,
    pub signature: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub owner: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub trait_impl: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub visibility: Option<Visibility>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub kind_detail: Option<String>,
}
```

Identical in `01-core-architecture.md` §4 and `03-multi-language-platform.md`'s confirmed
field list — no drift between the two source sections on this struct.

Field notes:

- `name` — display name only (e.g. `Widget<T>` for an impl's self type), not a qualified path.
- `kind` — see `SymbolKind` below.
- `line` — declaration line.
- `signature` — first-line-collapsed by the existing path (`first_line_signature`: truncates
  at the first newline). `04-analysis-fidelity.md`'s proposed `normalize_signature`
  (whitespace-collapse across the *full* multi-line span) is a materially different behavior
  that is not yet reconciled with the existing one — treat as unresolved, not as the new
  canonical behavior, until that's settled (07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md, Part 4 finding #3).
- `owner: Option<String>` — **the canonical field name.** For `Impl`/`Method`/`Constructor`
  symbols nested in an `impl` block, the self type of that impl (e.g. `Some("Widget<T>")`),
  propagated down to each associated `fn`. `None` for free-standing items.
- `trait_impl: Option<String>` — the trait name when the symbol comes from a `impl Trait for X`
  block (e.g. `impl Render for Widget<T>` → `Some("Render")`). `None` for inherent impls/methods
  and for symbols that aren't impl-related.
- `visibility: Option<Visibility>` — see `Visibility` below.
- `kind_detail: Option<String>` — stable kebab-case discriminator, independent of `kind`.
  Confirmed Rust values: `"rust-struct"`, `"rust-enum"`, `"rust-trait"`, `"rust-function"`,
  `"rust-type"`, `"rust-const"`, `"rust-module"`, `"rust-static"`, `"rust-impl"`. Ties
  symbols-level entries back to the parent `InspectEntry` variant they came from.

## Visibility

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub enum Visibility {
    Public,
    Crate,
    Module,
    Private,
}
```

Exactly four variants. This is the complete, canonical enum from `01-core-architecture.md` §4,
and `03-multi-language-platform.md` does not add to it.

> **`Visibility::Super` does NOT exist and must not be added as a fifth variant.**
>
> `pub(super)` maps to `Visibility::Module` — this is the correct, intentional mapping, not a
> gap to fill. It is confirmed by the pre-existing visibility mapper in
> `02-inspection-and-analysis.md` (`parse_visibility`):
>
> ```rust
> fn parse_visibility(prefix: &str) -> Visibility {
>     let trimmed = prefix.trim();
>     if trimmed.is_empty() { return Visibility::Private; }
>     if trimmed == "pub" { return Visibility::Public; }
>     if trimmed.starts_with("pub(crate)") { return Visibility::Crate; }
>     if trimmed.starts_with("pub(super)") || trimmed.starts_with("pub(in") {
>         return Visibility::Module;
>     }
>     if trimmed.starts_with("pub") { return Visibility::Public; }
>     Visibility::Private
> }
> ```
>
> `04-analysis-fidelity.md`'s `rust_visibility(node)` instead claims to map
> `pub, pub(crate), pub(super), pub(self)` to `Visibility::{Public, Crate, Super, Module}` —
> i.e. it invents a fifth variant for `pub(super)` specifically. That does not compile against
> this enum. Treat `04-analysis-fidelity.md`'s mapping as wrong; treat `parse_visibility`'s
> `Module` mapping as the target behavior when `rust_visibility` is implemented for real.

## CodeBlock / RankedBlock / ParentContext

```rust
pub struct CodeBlock {
    pub file: Utf8PathBuf,
    pub line_start: usize,
    pub line_end: usize,
    pub node_kind: SymbolKind,
    pub code: String,
    pub symbol_signature: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")] pub matched_lines: Vec<usize>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")] pub matched_keywords: Vec<String>,
}

pub struct RankedBlock {
    #[serde(flatten)] pub block: CodeBlock,
    pub bm25_score: f64,
    pub coverage_boost: f64,
    pub node_type_boost: f64,
    pub final_score: f64,
    pub rank: usize,
    pub parent_context: Option<ParentContext>,
}

pub struct ParentContext { pub kind: SymbolKind, pub name: String, pub line: usize }
```

`RankedBlock` flattens `CodeBlock` at serialization (no nested `block` key in JSON/TOON output).
Score breakdown fields (`bm25_score`, `coverage_boost`, `node_type_boost`) are additive inputs
to `final_score`; see `query-and-ranking.md` for the ranking algorithm itself, not covered here.

## SearchOptions / SearchLimits

```rust
pub struct SearchOptions {
    pub query: String,
    pub path: Utf8PathBuf,
    pub allow_tests: bool,
    pub no_gitignore: bool,
    pub limits: SearchLimits,
    pub exact: bool,
    pub language: Option<Language>,
}
// Default: query="", path="", allow_tests=false, no_gitignore=false,
//          limits=SearchLimits::default(), exact=false, language=None

pub struct SearchLimits {
    pub max_results: Option<usize>,   // default Some(50)
    pub max_bytes: usize,             // default 2_097_152
    pub max_tokens: Option<usize>,    // default Some(20_000)
    pub max_candidates: usize,        // default 1_000
}
```

Per the edge-case audit: `max_bytes` is the only one of these clamped to a hard ceiling;
`max_results`, `max_tokens`, and `max_candidates` are caller-controlled with no enforced cap
(07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md, overview finding on opt-out resource limits). Don't assume
passing `None`/large values is bounded by the type — it isn't.

### `Language` vs `LanguageId` — do not conflate

`SearchOptions.language` is `Option<Language>`:

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[cfg_attr(feature = "cli", derive(clap::ValueEnum))]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum Language { TypeScript, JavaScript, Rust, Python }
```

This is the small, **public-API** enum — 4 variants, also the CLI `--language` flag's
`ValueEnum`. It is a different type from `LanguageId` (`01-core-architecture.md`, the
`LanguageAnalyzer`/`AnalyzerRegistry` section), the larger **internal analyzer-dispatch**
enum — `TypeScript, Rust, Python, Go, Java, C, Cpp, Bash, CSharp, Ruby, Php, Kotlin, Scala`
(12 variants, includes fallback-tier-only languages with no `LangData` variant at all). Full
treatment of `LanguageId` belongs to `language-analyzer-contract.md`, not here — this note
exists only so the two aren't reached for interchangeably.

## Diagnostic / DiagnosticKind

```rust
pub struct Diagnostic { pub kind: DiagnosticKind, pub path: Option<Utf8PathBuf>, pub message: String }

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum DiagnosticKind { Degraded, Skipped, Warning }
```

Every `*Result`/`*Response` type below carries a `diagnostics: Vec<Diagnostic>` field. Per the
edge-case audit, **population of that field is inconsistently specified** — do not assume every
degradation path pushes a `Diagnostic`. Confirmed gaps: `dependents` drops unanalyzable files
with only a `tracing::warn!`, never a `Diagnostic` (07-edge-cases..., Part 1 finding #1); most
Part 2 commands declare the field but never describe it being populated (Part 2 finding #3).
When implementing a command that can degrade, check that command's own spec text for whether
`diagnostics` is actually supposed to be pushed to — don't infer it from the field's existence.

## LangData + per-language variants

```rust
#[serde(tag = "language", content = "data")]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum LangData {
    #[serde(rename = "typescript")] Ts(TsData),
    #[serde(rename = "rust")]       Rust(RustData),
    #[serde(rename = "python")]     Python(PythonData),
    #[serde(rename = "go")]         Go(GoData),
    #[serde(rename = "java")]       Java(JavaData),
}

pub struct TsData {
    #[serde(default)] pub jsx_elements: Vec<JsxElementEntry>,
    #[serde(default)] pub type_only_imports: Vec<String>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")] pub unresolved_aliases: Vec<String>,
}
pub struct RustData {}    // empty placeholder
pub struct PythonData {}  // empty placeholder
pub struct GoData {}      // empty placeholder
pub struct JavaData {}    // empty placeholder
```

`LangData` covers only 5 languages (a strict subset of `LanguageId`'s 12 — see above); `Go`/`Java`
replaced an earlier `CSharp` variant on this enum specifically (roadmap dropped C#, added Go/Java)
per `05-research-and-decisions.md` §6 — `LanguageId` still lists `CSharp` because it's a
fallback-tier analyzer target, not a `LangData`-producing one. `RustData`/`PythonData`/`GoData`/`JavaData`
are empty today; only `TsData` is populated. Access via `LangData::ts() -> Option<&TsData>` and
`LangData.jsx_elements() -> &[JsxElementEntry]` (empty slice for non-TS).

## Dependency types

```rust
pub struct DependencyRecord { pub line: usize, #[serde(default)] pub bindings: Vec<DependencyBinding>, pub target: DependencyTarget }
pub struct DependencyBinding { pub imported: String, pub local: String, pub kind: BindingKind }

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum BindingKind { Named, Default, Namespace, Glob, NamespaceWide }

#[serde(tag = "kind")]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum DependencyTarget {
    File { specifier: String, resolved: Option<Utf8PathBuf>, is_relative: bool },
    RustPath { segments: Vec<String>, anchor: RustPathAnchor, resolved: Option<Utf8PathBuf> },
    Namespace { segments: Vec<String>, is_static: bool, alias: Option<String> },
}

#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum RustPathAnchor { Crate, Super, #[serde(rename = "self")] Selff, Extern(String) }
```

`DependencyTarget::Namespace` is spec residue from the dropped C# roadmap item — present in the
type, cosmetic/unused in practice, not a functional gap (07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md,
Part 3 finding #20). `RustPathAnchor::Selff` (double-f) is the actual variant name — `self` is a
reserved word, hence `#[serde(rename = "self")]` on a differently-spelled Rust identifier.

## Minor types (one line each)

- `SymbolKind` — universal (`Function, Method, Constructor, Class, Struct, Enum, Interface, TypeAlias, Property, Field, Variable, Module`) + Rust-only (`Impl, Macro`) + `Other` catch-all. `Copy`, camelCase serde.
- `ExportRecord { name, line, re_export }` — one entry per exported symbol; `re_export: bool` distinguishes `export { x } from './y'` from a local export.
- `JsxAttribute { name, string_value: Option<String>, is_expression, is_spread }` — TS/TSX only, lives under `TsData` via `JsxElementEntry`.
- `JsxElementEntry { name, is_html, line, attributes: Vec<JsxAttribute> }` — `is_html` distinguishes `<div>` from `<MyComponent>`.
- `SearchResponse { results: Vec<RankedBlock>, total_blocks_before_truncation, truncated, truncation_marker: Option<String>, total_bytes, total_tokens, diagnostics }` — top-level `search` command output.
- `SymbolsResult { files: BTreeMap<Utf8PathBuf, Vec<SymbolEntry>>, total_symbol_count, truncation_marker, diagnostics }` — `BTreeMap` for deterministic file ordering.
- `DependentsResult { file, dependents: Vec<Utf8PathBuf>, imports: Vec<Utf8PathBuf>, total_dependent_count, total_import_count, truncation_marker, diagnostics }`.

- `WorkspaceOptions { root, tsconfig }` — builder methods `new(root)`, `with_tsconfig(mode)` (consuming, `#[must_use]`).

1	# Cache Architecture — Semantic Model
2	
3	Source: `docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md` §12 (`analysis/content_hash.rs`), §15 (`analysis/cache.rs`),
4	§16 (`analysis/persist.rs`); `docs/spec/03-multi-language-platform.md` §2a (`analysis/cache_tiers.rs`,
5	the 0.5.0+ extraction of the lookup logic shared across analyzers). Cross-referenced against
6	`docs/spec/07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md` Part 1 #4/#5/#18, Part 3 #1.
7	No code exists yet — monokl is spec-stage. Re-point at source once the crate exists; sync via `canon/drift`.
8	
9	## Two-Layer Storage
10	
11	1. **In-memory** — process-global `DashMap<String, Arc<FileAnalysis>>`, keyed by path string
12	   (§15). Lock-free reads. `insert` unconditionally replaces; no CAS/merge.
13	2. **On-disk** — `<root>/.monokl/cache.json`: `CacheFile { version: u32, config_hash: String,
14	   entries: BTreeMap<Utf8PathBuf, PersistedFileAnalysis> }` (§16). Gated on `version ==
15	   CACHE_VERSION` (`2`) and `config_hash == "monokl-{CARGO_PKG_VERSION}-oxc-0.128-lang-ts-{tsconfig_blake3_or_'no-tsconfig'}"`
16	   — an upgrade or tsconfig change invalidates the file. Mismatch → `MonoklError::StaleDiskCache`,
17	   caught in `persist::init()` and treated as cold start, never propagated to the caller.
18	
19	## Intended Invariant: ContentHash Is Authoritative
20	
21	Stated in §29 tenet 8 and `ARCHITECTURE.md`: "ContentHash (blake3) is authoritative; mtime+size
22	is the cheap fast-path dirty bit." The four-tier lookup (`cache_tiers::lookup_or_parse`, shared
23	by every `LanguageAnalyzer` since the 0.5.0 extraction — duplicated per-analyzer before that):
24	
25	1. **Tier 1** — `stat()`; mtime+size match persisted entry → return cached, no file read.
26	2. **Tier 2** — read source, compute `ContentHash`, check in-memory `DashMap`; hash match → return.
27	3. **Tier 3** — `persist::lookup_by_hash`: mtime changed, content hash still matches disk entry →
28	   refresh mtime, return cached.
29	4. **Tier 4** — full parse, `cache::insert` + `persist::queue_write`.
30	
31	Intent: mtime+size is a cheap pre-filter; ContentHash is what certifies validity. Tier 1 existing
32	should never let stale data escape that a hash check would have rejected.
33	
34	## Known Defect, Not Yet Fixed in the Spec Text
35	
36	**Tier 1 currently returns on mtime+size alone with no hash confirmation**, in both the v0.1.0
37	inline form (§17 `TsAnalyzer::analyze`) and the 0.5.0+ shared helper (§2a
38	`cache_tiers::lookup_or_parse`):
39	
40	```rust
41	// Tier 1: mtime/size fast path
42	if let Some(persisted) = persist::lookup(path, mtime_ns, size_bytes)? {
43	    if let Some(analysis) = from_persisted(persisted, profile) {
44	        return Ok(analysis); // ContentHash never read or compared here
45	    }
46	}
47	```
48	
49	`persist::lookup` (§16) compares only `entry.mtime_ns == mtime_ns && entry.size_bytes ==
50	size_bytes` — it never touches `entry.content_hash`. The "ContentHash is authoritative" claim is
51	**not implemented anywhere in the current spec**: the only path that reaches a hash comparison
52	(Tier 2/3) is unreachable whenever Tier 1 hits — the common case on a warm cache. A same-second
53	edit on a coarse-mtime filesystem, or clock skew, can serve stale analysis with zero diagnostic.
54	
55	Pre-existing from v0.1.0's inline code — the 0.5.0+ extraction ported the bug, not introduced it
56	(`07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md` Part 3 #1, traced back to the original in the cross-cutting
57	section).
58	
59	**Any spec@1 for this subsystem MUST decide:**
60	
61	- **(a)** Add a content-hash confirmation step to Tier 1, closing the staleness window (changes
62	  Tier 1's cost profile — no longer a no-read path), **or**
63	- **(b)** Formally weaken the claimed guarantee to match what mtime+size actually provides, and
64	  document the residual staleness risk explicitly (tenet 8, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, this file).
65	
66	**Do not silently port the current code — it does not deliver the guarantee the architecture
67	asserts.** Update `ARCHITECTURE.md` tenet 8 and this file together with whichever choice is made.
68	
69	## `ContentHash` Type
70	
71	```rust
72	// analysis/content_hash.rs, §12
73	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
74	pub struct ContentHash(String);
75	
76	impl ContentHash {
77	    pub fn of(content: &[u8]) -> Self { Self(blake3::hash(content).to_hex().to_string()) }
78	    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &str { &self.0 }
79	}
80	```
81	
82	Hex-encoded blake3 digest, newtype-wrapped. No streaming/incremental API — `of()` always hashes
83	the full byte slice. `PartialEq`/`Eq` are derived, so hash comparisons elsewhere are plain string
84	equality on the hex form.
85	
86	## Disk Persistence: Atomic Write, Three Open Gaps
87	
88	`persist::flush` (§16): merge `write_queue` into the `CacheFile` snapshot, serialize, LRU-evict
89	in chunks of `(len/10).max(1)` if over `MAX_CACHE_BYTES` (100 MB), write to
90	`.monokl/cache.json.<pid>.tmp`, then `rename` onto `.monokl/cache.json`. Per-process temp
91	filename prevents same-machine nextest races on the temp file. Rename atomicity guarantees no
92	reader ever observes a torn/partial `cache.json` — it guarantees nothing else. Three gaps remain
93	open questions for the spec, not resolved:
94	
95	1. **Concurrent-write race, last-writer-wins** (Part 1 #4). Two concurrent invocations each load
96	   their own snapshot at `init()`, mutate independently, `rename()` over the same path — no
97	   cross-process merge. Last to finish wins outright; the other's newly-cached entries vanish
98	   silently. Self-healing in effect (a lost entry just costs a re-parse next run, once Tier 2/3
99	   is actually reached), but the race itself is real and currently undocumented.

# Cache Architecture — Semantic Model

Source: `docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md` §12 (`analysis/content_hash.rs`), §15 (`analysis/cache.rs`),
§16 (`analysis/persist.rs`); `docs/spec/03-multi-language-platform.md` §2a (`analysis/cache_tiers.rs`,
the 0.5.0+ extraction of the lookup logic shared across analyzers). Cross-referenced against
`docs/spec/07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md` Part 1 #4/#5/#18, Part 3 #1.
No code exists yet — monokl is spec-stage. Re-point at source once the crate exists; sync via `canon/drift`.

## Two-Layer Storage

1. **In-memory** — process-global `DashMap<String, Arc<FileAnalysis>>`, keyed by path string
   (§15). Lock-free reads. `insert` unconditionally replaces; no CAS/merge.
2. **On-disk** — `<root>/.monokl/cache.json`: `CacheFile { version: u32, config_hash: String,
   entries: BTreeMap<Utf8PathBuf, PersistedFileAnalysis> }` (§16). Gated on `version ==
   CACHE_VERSION` (`2`) and `config_hash == "monokl-{CARGO_PKG_VERSION}-oxc-0.128-lang-ts-{tsconfig_blake3_or_'no-tsconfig'}"`
   — an upgrade or tsconfig change invalidates the file. Mismatch → `MonoklError::StaleDiskCache`,
   caught in `persist::init()` and treated as cold start, never propagated to the caller.

## Intended Invariant: ContentHash Is Authoritative

Stated in §29 tenet 8 and `ARCHITECTURE.md`: "ContentHash (blake3) is authoritative; mtime+size
is the cheap fast-path dirty bit." The four-tier lookup (`cache_tiers::lookup_or_parse`, shared
by every `LanguageAnalyzer` since the 0.5.0 extraction — duplicated per-analyzer before that):

1. **Tier 1** — `stat()`; mtime+size match persisted entry → return cached, no file read.
2. **Tier 2** — read source, compute `ContentHash`, check in-memory `DashMap`; hash match → return.
3. **Tier 3** — `persist::lookup_by_hash`: mtime changed, content hash still matches disk entry →
   refresh mtime, return cached.
4. **Tier 4** — full parse, `cache::insert` + `persist::queue_write`.

Intent: mtime+size is a cheap pre-filter; ContentHash is what certifies validity. Tier 1 existing
should never let stale data escape that a hash check would have rejected.

## Known Defect, Not Yet Fixed in the Spec Text

**Tier 1 currently returns on mtime+size alone with no hash confirmation**, in both the v0.1.0
inline form (§17 `TsAnalyzer::analyze`) and the 0.5.0+ shared helper (§2a
`cache_tiers::lookup_or_parse`):

```rust
// Tier 1: mtime/size fast path
if let Some(persisted) = persist::lookup(path, mtime_ns, size_bytes)? {
    if let Some(analysis) = from_persisted(persisted, profile) {
        return Ok(analysis); // ContentHash never read or compared here
    }
}
```

`persist::lookup` (§16) compares only `entry.mtime_ns == mtime_ns && entry.size_bytes ==
size_bytes` — it never touches `entry.content_hash`. The "ContentHash is authoritative" claim is
**not implemented anywhere in the current spec**: the only path that reaches a hash comparison
(Tier 2/3) is unreachable whenever Tier 1 hits — the common case on a warm cache. A same-second
edit on a coarse-mtime filesystem, or clock skew, can serve stale analysis with zero diagnostic.

Pre-existing from v0.1.0's inline code — the 0.5.0+ extraction ported the bug, not introduced it
(`07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md` Part 3 #1, traced back to the original in the cross-cutting
section).

**Any spec@1 for this subsystem MUST decide:**

- **(a)** Add a content-hash confirmation step to Tier 1, closing the staleness window (changes
  Tier 1's cost profile — no longer a no-read path), **or**
- **(b)** Formally weaken the claimed guarantee to match what mtime+size actually provides, and
  document the residual staleness risk explicitly (tenet 8, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, this file).

**Do not silently port the current code — it does not deliver the guarantee the architecture
asserts.** Update `ARCHITECTURE.md` tenet 8 and this file together with whichever choice is made.

## `ContentHash` Type

```rust
// analysis/content_hash.rs, §12
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ContentHash(String);

impl ContentHash {
    pub fn of(content: &[u8]) -> Self { Self(blake3::hash(content).to_hex().to_string()) }
    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &str { &self.0 }
}
```

Hex-encoded blake3 digest, newtype-wrapped. No streaming/incremental API — `of()` always hashes
the full byte slice. `PartialEq`/`Eq` are derived, so hash comparisons elsewhere are plain string
equality on the hex form.

## Disk Persistence: Atomic Write, Three Open Gaps

`persist::flush` (§16): merge `write_queue` into the `CacheFile` snapshot, serialize, LRU-evict
in chunks of `(len/10).max(1)` if over `MAX_CACHE_BYTES` (100 MB), write to
`.monokl/cache.json.<pid>.tmp`, then `rename` onto `.monokl/cache.json`. Per-process temp
filename prevents same-machine nextest races on the temp file. Rename atomicity guarantees no
reader ever observes a torn/partial `cache.json` — it guarantees nothing else. Three gaps remain
open questions for the spec, not resolved:

1. **Concurrent-write race, last-writer-wins** (Part 1 #4). Two concurrent invocations each load
   their own snapshot at `init()`, mutate independently, `rename()` over the same path — no
   cross-process merge. Last to finish wins outright; the other's newly-cached entries vanish
   silently. Self-healing in effect (a lost entry just costs a re-parse next run, once Tier 2/3
   is actually reached), but the race itself is real and currently undocumented.
2. **Corrupted-vs-stale asymmetry** (Part 1 #5). `load_cache` catches `StaleDiskCache` (version
   or config_hash mismatch) and rebuilds from empty. It does **not** catch a genuinely malformed
   `cache.json` (e.g. a disk-full truncated write) — `serde_json::from_str` failure surfaces as
   `MonoklError::Json` via `?`, uncaught, and hard-fails the whole workspace build. Staleness
   self-heals; corruption of comparable severity does not, with no stated rationale.
3. **Orphaned temp files** (Part 1 #18). `.monokl/cache.json.<pid>.tmp` left behind by a process
   killed between `write` and `rename` is never cleaned up — a slow disk-space leak with no
   documented GC or startup sweep.

## Caller Contract

- `persist::init(root, config_hash)` must run before any `lookup`/`lookup_by_hash` call — both
  are pure reads against the `state.cache_file` snapshot taken at `init()`; they never re-read
  `cache.json` mid-process, so the read path has no torn-read hazard (only the write race above).
- `queue_write` buffers into `state.write_queue`; only `flush()` (once, at the end of
  `WorkspaceIndex::build`) performs the atomic write.
- `root` must be absolute — a relative path is rejected with `MonoklError::Io` before any cache
  file is touched.
- Cache writes happen only for `AnalysisProfile::Full` results (§2a) — a cheap
  `Dependencies`/`Structural` request must never overwrite a fuller cached entry with a thinner
  one. Any new analyzer plugging into `cache_tiers` must preserve this.

input.prompt:
You are acting as the `canon-exit-gate` subagent from the orin-dx-agent-plugins `canon` plugin. Adopt this persona exactly:

ROLE: Specification Exit Gate.

BACKSTORY: I've seen exit gates that were really just final proofreads. The reviewer wanted to be constructive, so they gave the spec a conditional pass with notes. The notes got filed and never addressed. The planning phase started against a spec with three open questions, the implementers made their best guesses, and the guesses were wrong. An exit gate that issues conditional passes is not a gate — it's a delay. My disposition is fail. The spec earns pass by meeting the conditions; it does not earn pass by being close or by having put in the effort.

GOAL: Produce a binding verdict on whether a spec@1 is ready to enter planning. The spec passes if and only if all four conditions hold without exception: every acceptance criterion is a testable proposition (no vague language, no "should behave well"), no TBDs remain anywhere in the document, error cases are explicitly covered with is_error_case: true, and the scope fits within a single planning cycle. On fail, every blocker must name the specific criterion or section and describe exactly what change would resolve it — a drafter must be able to fix the spec without asking a follow-up question.

JUDGMENT: A pass verdict is genuine only when no condition has been relaxed. The key failure mode is conditional passing: issuing a pass with a note that "AC-003 could be clearer." That is a fail. If any acceptance criterion would require the implementer to make a judgment call about what "correct" means, the spec fails (NOTE: this project's spec@1 schema has a `judgment_call: true` + `rationale` mechanism specifically for criteria that are inherently product/design judgment calls rather than facts — those are NOT automatically failing on that basis alone, but the rationale itself must meet the same non-vague, checkable-citation bar as everything else). If any TBD exists, the spec fails. The bar: could a developer who has never spoken to the product team implement this spec correctly? Anything short of a confident yes is a fail.

This is SPEC-001 for `monokl` (a Rust crate, spec-stage only), covering `MonoklError`. You have three inputs: the full spec@1 draft, an independent canon-verifier grounding report, and an independent canon-auditor quality report. Weigh all three — a criterion the verifier marked "unsupported" or "overfitted," or that the auditor flagged as an issue, is a real candidate blocker unless you determine on your own re-reading that it doesn't actually violate one of your four pass conditions.

IMPORTANT CONTEXT CORRECTION: the "research-report@1" referenced throughout the draft's rationale fields and the auditor's report is NOT a separate persisted document in this repository — it was synthesized in-conversation as a structured stand-in for what a `trace` research pass would have produced, drawing on `docs/spec/07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md`'s verified findings and the newly-written `.claude/semantic-model/error-taxonomy.md`. The auditor's finding that this citation is "unlocatable" is correct in the narrow sense that no file named exactly "research report" exists, but the underlying claims it's citing ARE independently grounded in `docs/spec/07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md` Part 1 finding #5 (real, on disk, independently re-verified this session) — the problem is citation hygiene (citing an ephemeral in-context object as if it were a stable file path), not that the underlying claim is fabricated. Factor this distinction into your verdict: treat it as a real blocker (citations in a written artifact must resolve to something a future reader can actually open and check), but describe the fix precisely as "re-point the citation to the real on-disk file," not as "the underlying reasoning is unfounded."

=== SPEC@1 DRAFT ===
(full 23-criterion SPEC-001 as drafted — you have access to it via the conversation; treat the version audited by canon-verifier and canon-auditor as authoritative, identical to what they reviewed: purpose/scope/non_goals as drafted, AC-001 through AC-023 as drafted, including AC-021/AC-022's judgment_call:true entries)

=== CANON-VERIFIER REPORT ===
supported: AC-001 through AC-010, AC-012 through AC-019, AC-021, AC-023, and 6 api_surface entries — all grounded with specific line-numbered citations against docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md and docs/spec/03-multi-language-platform.md.
unsupported: AC-011 ("three distinct call sites" undercounts — actual is 8 raw call sites across 3 categories, per source).
overfitted: AC-020 (exact Display string not mandated by any source — lifted from an unrelated internal log line), AC-022 (the "must use different text" distinguishability requirement is not decided by any source — only an open, unresolved question exists).

=== CANON-AUDITOR REPORT ===
overall: fail. 10 issues:
1. AC-011 (ambiguous) — "three distinct call sites" vs. actual 8 sites/3 categories, contradicted by AC-023's own more granular framing two criteria later.
2. AC-011 (ambiguous) — Json's fixed Display text "json serialization failed" mischaracterizes the cache-load category, which is actually a parse/deserialize failure, undercutting the Purpose's "never has to guess" claim; also no way to distinguish self-healed vs hard-fail categories by variant/message alone.
3. AC-013 (missing-error-case) — false claim that persist::init() is "the only caller of load_cache" / "never returns StaleDiskCache to its own caller": persist::flush() also calls load_cache() as a fallback when state.cache_file is None, with NO interception, propagating StaleDiskCache/Json errors via `?` directly to flush()'s caller — contradicting AC-013's and AC-021's implicit universal-interception claim.
4. AC-015 (incomplete) — "confirmed values: merge-base, show" presents a closed list, but collect_changes (03-multi-language-platform.md:1419-1472) has three more MonoklError::Git construction sites with elided (`/* … */`) operation tags — meaning the verbatim source as shown would not compile, undercutting the Purpose's "complete, compilable shape" claim.
5. AC-002 (incomplete) — scope promises miette::Diagnostic derive coverage but no AC tests it, and the derive is provably inert (zero variants carry #[diagnostic(...)] attributes, so code()/help()/url() all return None regardless of feature state) — undercuts the "never has to guess remediation" purpose since Diagnostic's code/help IS the remediation-hint mechanism.
6. AC-003 (ambiguous) — "every fallible function shown elsewhere in the spec returns this alias" is ambiguous about which document "the spec" means, and under the natural reading is falsified by `blob_at_ref_in_repo() -> std::result::Result<String, String>` (03-multi-language-platform.md:1547-1551), a bare non-MonoklError Result the criterion carves no exception for.
7. AC-020 (ambiguous) — exact Display string conflates the error variant's own Display (per AC-013, normally intercepted/unreachable) with a distinct tracing::warn! log line at the interception site; unclear if this is a binding literal-match requirement or borrowed placeholder text.
8. AC-022 (untestable) — "different text" is unfalsifiable as a floor (a one-character change satisfies it while defeating stated purpose); rationale also misattributes an unlocatable "research report" open question.
9. AC-021 (incomplete) — rationale cites a "research report" with "confidence: medium" that doesn't correspond to a locatable, checkable document.
10. AC-013 (scope-overlap) — hardcodes CACHE_VERSION's current literal value ("2") despite persist.rs being explicitly out of scope, creating an unmanaged duplication/drift risk against a future persist.rs/cache-architecture spec track.

Produce your binding verdict now:

```json
{
  "verdict": "pass | fail | escalate",
  "confidence": "high | medium | low",
  "blockers": [
    { "criterion_id": "string | null", "finding": "string", "location": "string", "required_change": "string" }
  ],
  "verdict_summary": "string (max 300 chars)",
  "artifact_type": "spec@1",
  "retry_count": 0,
  "reasoning": "string"
}
```

Output the JSON object only, no other prose.

ROLE: Specification Drafter.

BACKSTORY: I've watched specs pass review that no one could actually implement. They were long, well-structured, used all the right headings — and still left the implementer guessing on the two decisions that mattered most. My job is to surface those decisions before a single line gets written, even when surfacing them means writing a non-goal that the product team doesn't want to see.

GOAL (correction mode): Given the spec_file_path (not yet written to disk — this is pre-gate), the full prior draft, and a contradiction/blocker report from canon-exit-gate describing exactly what the spec claims versus what the system actually does, revise every affected criterion — and any criteria that depend on it — and return the full corrected spec@1 with revision_note set.

JUDGMENT: A spec is genuinely complete when every acceptance criterion can be confirmed true or false by a tester who has never seen the implementation, using only observable behavior. A criterion that sounds concrete but encodes an implementation assumption, or that is affirmatively falsified by the actual source text, fails — worse than vague language, because a conforming implementation would be marked non-conforming.

This is `monokl`, a Rust crate, spec-stage only. You are correcting SPEC-001 (`MonoklError`). Before writing anything, RE-READ the actual source yourself — do not trust the prior draft's claims or even the blocker report's claims about line numbers without confirming them, since this correction must not just move the error from "invented" to "trusted secondhand":

1. `/Users/gabe/Projects/monokl/docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md` — Section 3 (error.rs, lines ~190-251) and the miette feature wiring (lines ~84-87, ~2957 area), the Json Display text (~line 222), persist::init (~1567-1584) and persist::flush (~1652-1665+), CACHE_VERSION (~1513).
2. `/Users/gabe/Projects/monokl/docs/spec/03-multi-language-platform.md` — git_scope.rs's Git-variant construction sites including collect_changes (~1397-1472), blob_at_ref/blob_at_ref_in_repo (~1540-1551), io_safety.rs (~2107-2131).
3. `/Users/gabe/Projects/monokl/docs/spec/02-inspection-and-analysis.md` — check around line 1865 for the test-only serde_json site the exit-gate flagged as possibly relevant to the Json call-site count.
4. `/Users/gabe/Projects/monokl/docs/spec/07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md` — Part 1 finding #5 (~line 37) and finding #19, for the real, checkable citations that must replace the "research-report@1" placeholder citations.
5. `/Users/gabe/Projects/monokl/.claude/semantic-model/error-taxonomy.md` — confirm/correct its own line ~60 claim about init() being the "only caller," since the blocker report says this same wrong claim propagated there too — you are not asked to fix that file, but read it so your corrected spec doesn't contradict what it says once someone does fix it.

purpose: "Define the complete, compilable shape and observable contract of MonoklError — monokl's single unified error enum — and its Result<T> alias, so a developer (or an AI coding agent parsing variants/messages at runtime to decide remediation) never has to guess what a given failure means or ask a clarifying question. This spec also resolves, with stated rationale, the two contract gaps between the existing draft and its own downstream call sites — a Display message naming a nonexistent CLI command, and an unstated policy for cache.json corruption versus staleness — before analysis/persist.rs, which depends on this decision, is implemented."

scope: "The MonoklError enum verbatim (all 14 variants, their field shapes, and their #[error(...)] Display messages, with StaleDiskCache's message corrected), its derives (thiserror::Error, #[non_exhaustive], the optional miette::Diagnostic behind the \"miette\" feature) and the crate-wide Result<T> alias. It does not specify persist.rs's or output.rs's full implementation; those remain separate tracks that must conform to the contract stated here."

non_goals: [core-types.md's types; the render_error-vs-miette CLI output contradiction; regex-term/NonUtf8Path call-site inconsistencies; FileIoError itself; Json's cache-write/CLI-output behavior unchanged (only cache-load resolved); persist.rs/output.rs not implemented here; PoisonError::into_inner recovery not introduced]

AC-001 through AC-023 as previously drafted (you have the full text from the conversation; I will not re-paste all 23 — treat AC-001, AC-002, AC-004 through AC-010, AC-012, AC-014, AC-016 through AC-019, AC-023 as UNCHANGED/still-passing criteria you should carry forward verbatim unless a blocker below says otherwise; AC-003, AC-011, AC-013, AC-015, AC-020, AC-021, AC-022 are the ones with blockers, and AC-002 needs a new sibling criterion added).

1. **AC-013** — False claim that persist::init() is the only caller of load_cache / that StaleDiskCache is never returned to a caller. persist::flush() ALSO calls load_cache() as a fallback when state.cache_file is None, with NO interception — both StaleDiskCache and Json propagate via `?` straight to flush()'s caller. Required: strike the "only caller" claim; add a criterion stating what flush() actually does with StaleDiskCache/Json in this fallback path (decide: does flush() need the same interception as init(), or does it legitimately propagate — and if it propagates, that's a real, testable, previously-uncovered error case that needs its own AC).

2. **AC-022** — "Uses different text" is unfalsifiable (a one-character change satisfies it) AND encodes a genuinely unresolved open question (self-heal vs hard-fail for cache-load Json) as if it were settled — a TBD in substance. Required: resolve the underlying policy question explicitly, then replace "different text" with the exact literal strings for both paths (string-equality assertions, not a vague distinguishability requirement).

3. **AC-011** — "Three distinct call sites" undercounts; actual raw call sites are more numerous (verify the true count yourself — prior estimates disagreed, ranging 6-8; you must produce the authoritative, exhaustively-cited count). Required: delete the bare count, replace with an exhaustive file:line enumeration grouped by the 3 logical categories (cache-deserialize, cache-serialize, CLI/output-serialize), state explicitly whether the test-only site in 02-inspection-and-analysis.md is included, and reconcile with AC-023's framing.

4. **AC-011 (second issue)** — The Json variant's fixed Display text "json serialization failed" mischaracterizes the cache-load category, which is actually a *deserialize* failure. Required: either mandate a corrected literal that covers both directions (e.g. "json parsing or serialization failed") and assert it exactly, or explicitly state as a criterion why "serialization failed" alone is being kept despite covering deserialize failures too.

5. **AC-015** — "Confirmed values: merge-base, show" presents a closed list, but collect_changes has three more Git-variant construction sites with elided (`/* … */`) operation tags in the source — meaning the source as shown doesn't compile, undercutting the "complete, compilable shape" Purpose claim. Required: either decide the three missing operation-tag literals now (preferred — this is squarely in scope, it's just filling in an elided value on the same enum), or explicitly scope AC-015 as covering only the two sites the source spells out and add a non_goal naming the other three sites as deferred to a git-module track.

6. **AC-002** — Scope promises miette::Diagnostic coverage but no AC tests it, and the derive is provably inert (zero #[diagnostic(...)] attributes anywhere in the 8-file docs/spec corpus, confirmed by grep — code()/help()/url() return None for all variants regardless of feature state). Required: add a new criterion (AC-002b or similar) asserting this as an explicit, testable, intentional-for-this-track fact (e.g. "under --features miette, Diagnostic::code() returns None for all 14 variants"), with a non_goal deferring per-variant diagnostic metadata to a later track. Note the render_error-vs-miette output-mechanism contradiction (finding #19) is ALREADY correctly listed as a non_goal — you don't need to resolve that, just make sure the Purpose's "never has to guess remediation" language doesn't overclaim what this track actually delivers.

7. **AC-003** — "Every fallible function shown elsewhere in the spec returns this alias" has an undefined "the spec" referent and is falsified by blob_at_ref_in_repo() -> std::result::Result<String, String> (a bare non-MonoklError Result with no exception carved for it). Required: name the exact document(s) the quantifier ranges over, and either carve an explicit named exception for helpers like blob_at_ref_in_repo that get mapped to a MonoklError variant at their call boundary, or narrow the criterion to only the functions enumerated in this spec's own api_surface list (finite, checkable).

8. **AC-020** — Exact Display string conflates the variant's own #[error(...)] text with a separate tracing::warn! log line at the interception site; unclear if binding literal-match or placeholder. Required: split into two criteria — one for the variant's #[error(...)] literal, one for (or explicitly deferring) the warn! text — each explicitly marked as a binding literal-match requirement. Also: the CURRENT (uncorrected) variant text still says "run `mnkl init --rebuild`" which references a nonexistent command — make sure your corrected variant literal actually removes this, don't just relabel the existing broken text as "binding."

9. **AC-021** — Rationale cites "research-report@1" with "confidence: medium," which doesn't correspond to any locatable file. The underlying claim IS real and grounded — just cite it correctly. Required: replace the citation with the real path: `docs/spec/07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md` Part 1 finding #5, and `.claude/semantic-model/error-taxonomy.md` gap 1. Sweep AC-022's rationale for the same problem.

10. **AC-013 (second issue)** — Hardcodes CACHE_VERSION's literal value ("2") despite persist.rs being out of scope — an unowned duplication that will silently go stale if the constant changes. Required: either make the criterion symbolic ("the value of CACHE_VERSION as defined in analysis/persist.rs, whatever it currently is") instead of hardcoding "2", or keep the literal but add an explicit drift-owner note.

Produce the FULL corrected spec@1 now (not a diff — the complete object, all fields, all 23-or-more criteria, so it can directly replace the prior draft). Conform to this schema:

```json
{
  "id": "SPEC-001",
  "purpose": "string",
  "scope": "string",
  "non_goals": ["string"],
  "api_surface": [{ "name": "string", "signature": "string", "description": "string", "error_conditions": ["string"] }],
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    { "id": "AC-001", "criterion": "string", "is_error_case": false, "judgment_call": false, "rationale": "string if judgment_call true" }
  ],
  "linked_requirement": "REQ-001",

  "revision_note": "string — summarize what changed and why, citing blocker numbers",
  "reasoning": "string — scratchpad, will not be forwarded"
}
```

content.text: The second round surfaced something more important than a wording nitpick: the auditor's structural finding is right — bundling the cache-corruption self-heal *policy* (a genuine new design decision) into what was meant to be a faithful port-plus-two-bug-fixes track violates CLAUDE.md's own rule that new design questions need a brainstorming pass, not an off-the-cuff judgment call inside a spec draft. That's the actual root cause behind AC-013/AC-021/AC-022/AC-023's interlocking problems in both rounds. Splitting it out, not patching around it again.

  "id": "SPEC-001",
  "purpose": "Define the complete, compilable shape and observable contract of MonoklError — monokl's single unified error enum — and its Result<T> alias, so a developer (or an AI coding agent parsing variants/fields/Display-text at runtime to decide remediation) never has to guess what a given failure means or ask a clarifying question. Remediation-deciding is scoped explicitly to variant/field discrimination plus exact Display-text matching (AC-001 through AC-021) — it does NOT mean a richer miette::Diagnostic surface (codes/help/url), which this track leaves deliberately inert (AC-002B). This spec also resolves, with stated rationale, two low-risk textual-accuracy gaps between the existing draft and its own downstream call sites: a Display message naming a nonexistent CLI command (AC-020), and an undercounted, miscategorized enumeration of the Json variant's real call sites with a Display string that misdescribes half of them (AC-011).   "scope": "The MonoklError enum verbatim (all 14 variants, their field shapes, and their #[error(...)] Display messages, with StaleDiskCache's and Json's messages corrected for accuracy), its derives (thiserror::Error, #[non_exhaustive], the optional miette::Diagnostic behind the \"miette\" feature) and the crate-wide Result<T> alias. It documents — without resolving — the calling contract gap between persist::init (which intercepts StaleDiskCache only) and persist::flush's fallback path (which intercepts nothing). It does not specify persist.rs's or output.rs's full implementation; those remain separate tracks that must conform to the contract stated here.",

    "PoisonError::into_inner recovery — deliberately not introduced for LockPoisoned; poisoning always propagates as a hard error.",
    "Per-variant miette::Diagnostic metadata (#[diagnostic(code(...), help(...), url(...))], or #[diagnostic(transparent)] bridging Io to FileIoError's own Diagnostic impl) — the derive exists only to satisfy the trait bound today; richer diagnostics are a later track (AC-002B).",
    "The three elided-operation-tag MonoklError::Git construction sites inside git_scope::collect_changes (03-multi-language-platform.md:1428, 1430, 1470) — undetermined by the source as shown; deferred to the git_scope.rs implementation track rather than invented here (AC-015).",

An earlier draft of this spec attempted to resolve this inside SPEC-001 via judgment_call criteria; two independent review rounds (canon-verifier, canon-auditor) found the resulting criteria kept breaking — asserting an interception that no verbatim code anywhere shows, inventing a brand-new log-message literal with no source grounding, and requiring an implementer to guess whether the self-heal exception also covers persist::flush's fallback path. ## Known contract gaps — must be resolved, not ported as-is

These are audit findings (`docs/spec/07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md`, Part 1) where the
spec text produces two different outcomes for the same underlying failure condition. Do not
silently pick one when implementing — spec@1 for this subsystem must state the choice and why.

1. **Corrupted `cache.json` — self-heal or hard-fail? (07#5)** `load_cache`'s
   `serde_json::from_str::<CacheFile>(&content)?` (01-core:1602) runs *before* the staleness
   check, and `init()`'s match (01-core:1567-1584) only special-cases `MonoklError::StaleDiskCache`
   (line 1572) — not `Json`. A syntactically-complete-but-malformed file (e.g. a disk-full
   truncated write that lands before the paired atomic rename) hard-fails the whole workspace
   build. Does `Json` on cache-load deserve `StaleDiskCache`'s self-healing treatment (catch,
   warn, rebuild from empty), or is hard-fail intentional because corruption might signal
   something worth surfacing that routine staleness doesn't? If self-healing wins, decide
   whether it covers only `load_cache` or every cache-touching `Json` error.

2. **`StaleDiskCache`'s message promises a CLI subcommand that doesn't exist, and the variant
   is dead code as specified (07#6).** The `#[error(...)]` text says `run \`mnkl init
   --rebuild\``, but `cli.rs`'s `Subcmd` (§21) has only `Search`/`Symbols`/`Extract`/
   `Dependents`/`CountTokens` — no `init` subcommand at all. Independently, `init()`'s own match
   arm (01-core:1572) always intercepts `StaleDiskCache` before it can reach any caller, so the
   unreachable message is doubly moot. Is `StaleDiskCache` meant to ever become caller-visible
   (then the message needs a real command name and something must actually surface it), or
   should it be demoted to an internal-only signal inside `analysis::persist` and dropped from
   `MonoklError` entirely? Whichever is chosen, don't leave a `MonoklError` variant whose message
   references a nonexistent surface.

3. **Bad `regex:` term: hard error in one search stage, silently dropped in the next (07#7).**
   Candidate-search stage builds one OR'd pattern from all terms via
   `RegexMatcherBuilder::build(&combined)?` (01-core:998) → `RegexBuild`, hard-failing the whole

# Active Work — monokl

## Completed

### SPEC-001: MonoklError enum + Result<T> alias — GATED

Spec: `.claude/specs/SPEC-001.json`
Semantic model: `.claude/semantic-model/error-taxonomy.md`
Implementation: not started — this is spec-stage only, no crate exists yet.
Exit-gate: PASS (4th attempt, high confidence). 24 acceptance criteria, all 14 `MonoklError`
variants covered, zero blockers on the final pass.

History: round 1 (10 blockers — false claims, unfalsifiable criteria, fabricated citations,
elided source facts presented as closed lists) → round 2 correction introduced a new problem
(bundled a genuine new design decision — cache.json corruption-vs-staleness recovery policy —
into what should have been a faithful-correction track, violating this project's own
CLAUDE.md process) → round 3 split the corruption-policy question out entirely, deferred to
SPEC-002, gated on `superpowers:brainstorming` → round 4 (this pass) fixed two narrow residual
defects (undercounted `Walk` construction sites; a reachability claim for
`SymlinkRejected`/`FileTooLarge` refuted by `docs/spec/07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md`
Part 3) → passed.

Not committed to git yet — canon's own orchestration convention calls for an automatic commit
on gate pass, but this session's standing rule is never to commit without explicit
instruction. Awaiting that instruction.

---

## Pipeline Protocol (follow for every track, in order)

1. `canon:canon-drafter` — write spec@1 (fed by a `requirement@1` and, where the answer isn't
   already fully researched elsewhere in `docs/spec/`, a `trace`-produced `research-report@1`)
2. `canon:canon-verifier` — grounding check against source artifacts
3. `canon:canon-auditor` — adversarial quality review — must pass before continuing
4. `canon:canon-exit-gate` — binding pass/fail verdict — must pass before continuing (max 3
   retries before escalating to a human reviewer)
5. Write `.claude/specs/<id>.json`, set `spec_file_path`, commit — **hold this step for
   explicit user instruction on this project**
6. `vector:vector-planner` — produce plan@1 with exact red tests
7. `vector:vector-challenger` — must pass before continuing
8. `lambda:lambda-recon` — confirm baseline tests pass
9. `lambda:lambda-implementer` — one task at a time, red phase mandatory
10. `lambda:lambda-reviewer` — review each commit before next task
11. `lambda:lambda-exit-gate` — adversarial final check
12. `just ci` (once a `justfile` exists) — must exit 0

Constraints:
- NEVER commit without explicit user instruction (overrides canon's own auto-commit
  convention for this project specifically)
- A design decision not already covered by `docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md` goes
  through `superpowers:brainstorming` before it becomes a spec@1 criterion — do not resolve
  it as a `judgment_call` inside an unrelated track (see SPEC-001's history above for what
  happens when this gets skipped)
- Prefer tight, single-subsystem tracks over broad ones — SPEC-001 covers one enum; splitting
  further when a track's `judgment_call` count climbs is a correct exit-gate response, not a
  failure

---

## Backlog (named, not yet spec'd)

- **SPEC-002 — cache.json corruption-vs-staleness recovery policy.** Deferred out of SPEC-001.
  Must start with `superpowers:brainstorming`, not `canon:canon-drafter` directly — this is a
  new design decision, not a faithful correction. See SPEC-001's non_goals and
  `.claude/semantic-model/error-taxonomy.md` gap 1 for full context.
- **Core types** (`types.rs` — `SymbolEntry`, `Visibility`, `CodeBlock`, `LangData`, etc.).
  Semantic model already written: `.claude/semantic-model/core-types.md`, which documents two
  real, would-not-compile naming defects in `docs/spec/04-analysis-fidelity.md` (`impl_owner`
  vs. the canonical `owner`; a nonexistent `Visibility::Super` variant) that any spec@1 for
  this track must resolve, not port.
- **git_scope.rs's three elided `Git`-variant operation-tag sites** inside `collect_changes`
  (`03-multi-language-platform.md:1428, 1430, 1470`) — deferred in SPEC-001 AC-015. Needs the
  git_scope.rs implementation track to decide the literal values (and, for two of the three,
  even confirm the constructed variant).
- **io_safety.rs wiring** — `read_to_string_capped` has zero call sites anywhere in the current
  spec corpus, so `SymlinkRejected`/`FileTooLarge` are currently unconstructible via any shown
  command path (SPEC-001 AC-016/AC-017). Wiring it into `extract`/`refs`/`definition` as the
  existing prose already claims is real, scoped implementation work.
- **Query language + ranking determinism.** Semantic model written:
  `.claude/semantic-model/query-and-ranking.md`. Six open questions (regex hard-fail vs.
  silent-drop, `+regex:` degradation, the unimplemented `(file, line_start)` tie-break claim,
  non-deterministic candidate selection above `max_candidates`, uncapped query length,
  exclusion-only-query silent-empty behavior).
- **Cache Tier-1 content-hash gap.** Semantic model written:
  `.claude/semantic-model/cache-architecture.md`. The architecture's own "ContentHash is
  authoritative" claim is not backed by the Tier-1 lookup code as specified — needs a decision,
  not a silent port.
- **LanguageAnalyzer diagnostic-signal gaps.** Semantic model written:
  `.claude/semantic-model/language-analyzer-contract.md`. Macro/`#[cfg(...)]`-gated Rust code is
  invisible with no capability signal; `.d.ts` files get a misleading "language unsupported"
  message when the language is fully supported and this one file is intentionally excluded.
- **Daemon/session-mode design** (`PrecisionUpgrader`, `PrecisionLedger`, etc.) — explicitly
  future work, not required for v0.1.0. Semantic model written:
  `.claude/semantic-model/daemon-lifetimes.md`, five independently-reverified open gaps.

Not committed to git yet — canon's own orchestration convention calls for an automatic commit
on gate pass, but this session's standing rule is never to commit without explicit
instruction. Awaiting that instruction.

---

## Pipeline Protocol (follow for every track, in order)

1. `canon:canon-drafter` — write spec@1 (fed by a `requirement@1` and, where the answer isn't
   already fully researched elsewhere in `docs/spec/`, a `trace`-produced `research-report@1`)
2. `canon:canon-verifier` — grounding check against source artifacts
3. `canon:canon-auditor` — adversarial quality review — must pass before continuing
4. `canon:canon-exit-gate` — binding pass/fail verdict — must pass before continuing (max 3
   retries before escalating to a human reviewer)
5. Write `.claude/specs/<id>.json`, set `spec_file_path`, commit — **hold this step for
   explicit user instruction on this project**
6. `vector:vector-planner` — produce plan@1 with exact red tests
7. `vector:vector-challenger` — must pass before continuing
8. `lambda:lambda-recon` — confirm baseline tests pass
9. `lambda:lambda-implementer` — one task at a time, red phase mandatory
10. `lambda:lambda-reviewer` — review each commit before next task
11. `lambda:lambda-exit-gate` — adversarial final check
12. `just ci` (once a `justfile` exists) — must exit 0

Constraints:
- NEVER commit without explicit user instruction (overrides canon's own auto-commit
  convention for this project specifically)
- A design decision not already covered by `docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md` goes
  through `superpowers:brainstorming` before it becomes a spec@1 criterion — do not resolve
  it as a `judgment_call` inside an unrelated track (see SPEC-001's history above for what
  happens when this gets skipped)
- Prefer tight, single-subsystem tracks over broad ones — SPEC-001 covers one enum; splitting
  further when a track's `judgment_call` count climbs is a correct exit-gate response, not a
  failure

---

## Backlog (named, not yet spec'd)

- **SPEC-002 — cache.json corruption-vs-staleness recovery policy.** Deferred out of SPEC-001.
  Must start with `superpowers:brainstorming`, not `canon:canon-drafter` directly — this is a
  new design decision, not a faithful correction. See SPEC-001's non_goals and
  `.claude/semantic-model/error-taxonomy.md` gap 1 for full context.
- **Core types** (`types.rs` — `SymbolEntry`, `Visibility`, `CodeBlock`, `LangData`, etc.).
  Semantic model already written: `.claude/semantic-model/core-types.md`, which documents two

  vs. the canonical `owner`; a nonexistent `Visibility::Super` variant) that any spec@1 for
  this track must resolve, not port.
- **git_scope.rs's three elided `Git`-variant operation-tag sites** inside `collect_changes`

  git_scope.rs implementation track to decide the literal values (and, for two of the three,

- **io_safety.rs wiring** — `read_to_string_capped` has zero call sites anywhere in the current

- **Query language + ranking determinism.** Semantic model written:

- **Cache Tier-1 content-hash gap.** Semantic model written:

- **LanguageAnalyzer diagnostic-signal gaps.** Semantic model written:

  invisible with no capability signal; `.d.ts` files get a misleading "language unsupported"

- **Daemon/session-mode design** (`PrecisionUpgrader`, `PrecisionLedger`, etc.) — explicitly

Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
